the drivers side front door from the silver toyota pushed against it. while investigating the situation, a silver 2002 chevrolet l/p [identifier] pulled up with damage on both the drivers side and passenger side rear bumper and quarter panels. the driver was courtney doucette b/f [date]. courtney said her vehicle was parked beside the other two vehicles and it was hit by another vehicle, that pushed courtney's vehicle into the silver toyota. the investigation revealed that vehicle 1 a black 2018 honda civic l/p temp tag 67588l1 was parked beside the three vehicles. vehicle 1 was driven by raul hearn w/m [date]. raul was involved in an altercation with a b/m identified as terrence hightower who pointed a weapon at raul. raul jumped in vehicle 1 and backed out of the parking spot when the weapon was pointed at him. terrence jumped in front of vehicle 1 and pointed the weapon at raul the second time. raul ducked behind the dash of the car, and punched the gas of the vehicle. raul was unable to turn the steering wheel and he hit terrence's leg with the bumper of the vehicle 1 against vehicle 2 as raul punched the gas to get out of the parking lot. vehicle 1 then hit vehicle 2 the 2002 silver chevrolet on the passenger rear bumper and quarter panel. vehicle 2 was pushed against vehicle 3 a silver 2013 toyota l/p [identifier]. vehicle 3 was pushed into vehicle 4 a tan 2013 kia sol. vehicle 3 was pushed up on the sidewalk and the drivers side rear bumper struck the drivers side door to vehicle 4. vehicle 1 continued on out of the parking lot and left the scene, due to deputies and given his side of the story. the owners to vehicle 3 and vehicle 4 were located and they were given the information on vehicle 1 and the driver. the owner of vehicle 2 was on scene and unlawful possession of firearm by felon.

records.deidentified_narrative: unit 1 was towing unit 2 traveling southbound on sh 79. the driver stated that there was a pedestrian [roadway], on or near the yellow center line. the driver stated that the pedestrian was jumping up and down and waving his arms in the air. the driver thought the pedestrian had been involved in crash and needed help. the driver slowed down and stopped on the right shoulder of sh 79. the pedestrian came up to the left side of the truck tractor, jumped on the steps and tried to open the door, but it was locked. the driver stated that the pedestrian was yelling and hitting the side of the truck tractor. the driver stated that the pedestrian repeatedly yelled, ""i didn't do it!, i didn't do it!"". the driver stated that the pedestrian was acting erratic and had the appearance of being under the influence of a drug or drugs. the pedestrian then went to the passenger side and tried to open the door, but it was also locked. the driver saw the pedestrian get down and move away from the truck [roadway] away. the driver stated that he felt the rear [roadway] over something and he stopped. the driver stated that he had not seen the pedestrian come back to his truck tractor. it is unclear why the pedestrian came back to the truck tractor. the truck tractor semi trailer came to a stop on the right shoulder of the roadway facing southwest. the pedestrian was lying on the grass in the barrow ditch just behind the truck tractor with his head close to the right tire of axle 3. the pedestrian's pelvis and legs had been crushed. the pedestrian refused to talk with me while i was on scene. during a phone conversation the pedestrian stated that he asked the driver for a ride to olney. the pedestrian stated that the driver did not respond and that he assumed that meant yes. the pedestrian stated that he did not get on the steps of the truck tractor. the pedestrian stated that as he was walking around the front of the truck tractor it started to move forward. the pedestrian stated that all the tires on the right side of the truck tractor, including the semi-trailer went over him. the pedestrian admitted that he had last used meth on saturday, april 25, 2020. based on the interviews and the evidence at the scene it is this investigators opinion that the account of the truck driver (unit #1) is the most accurate and plausible sequence of events.

records.deidentified_narrative: unit 1 was stationary, [roadway] nearest the curb, in the [roadway], facing northbound. unit 1 was waiting at the red light at the [roadway] [roadway] of ih-20. unit 1 was directly behind a pedal cyclist. unit 2 was a pedestrian, entering the marked crosswalk to walk northbound in the [roadway]. unit 1 advised the light turned green for northbound traffic and the cyclist was having trouble starting off in front of him. the driver of unit 1 advised the cyclist was ""wobbly"" and distracted the driver of unit 1. unit 1 made a right turn from the [roadway] into the [roadway] for ih-20. unit 2 advised she entered the marked crosswalk on a white ""walk"" indicator for northbound pedestrian traffic. unit 1 failed to yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian in a crosswalk and struck unit 2. witness: jasson speir [phone] advised he observed the crash occur but was traveling southbound, under ih-20, and therefore did not observe what color the traffic light or cross indicators were. he advised other witnesses, which departed the scene prior to my arrival, advised him the light for unit 1 was green. i did observed, after the scene was cleared, that the white walk signal for northbound pedestrian traffic does illuminate (when button at intersection is pressed) when the green light for northbound traffic illuminates. this is consistent with each account that both unit 1 had a green light and unit 2 had a white walk signal. mcdonald's (5090 ih-20, [roadway]) camera footage did capture the crash, from a distance. the footage does not capture any signal indicator light but only the crash. footage is very grainy when zoomed in and does not provide any new information that is not consistent with each units account. footage was documented on my body worn camera on [date] at approximately 1544 hours. no other establishment, in the area, captured the crash.
